lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet is a luxury in Toronto, and this front office has spent the summer proving it can be noisy without making a racket. John Chayka enters his first training camp Wednesday after a frantic offseason - one that left the Leafs remade in the corners and under the microscope at the crease. The season is over, the record is history, and now the real work begins: turn last year's mess into something sturdier. Anthony Stolarz is the hinge. If he can rebound from a 10-10-3 line and a.893 save percentage, the Leafs can breathe; if not, the goal crease stays a problem. Chayka says the club has already done its heavy lifting. Fine. Now it has to look like it. The next test is camp, where roster spots, roles and credibility get sorted in a hurry.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The winter's work is already pressing harder than the autumn's memory. Toronto's bullpen and rotation health will define the whole show, and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s first home run at Rogers Centre this season in Sunday's 8-1 win over Baltimore was the kind of jolt that reminds a club what power looks like when it finally wakes up. The Blue Jays finished 75-75, a perfectly ordinary record that screams for better pitching, and the injury list is crowded enough to make a trainer wince - Trey Yesavage is still working back from knee trouble, while Shane Bieber and Anthony Santander remain question marks. Guerrero's bat has to anchor the lineup, but the larger task is sturdier arms and fewer patchwork nights. What to watch next: how aggressively Toronto repairs the pitching staff before camp opens and whether its injury pile can be trimmed before spring.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet can be deceptive in the NBA, and Toronto's calm has a rattling edge to it. RJ Barrett will have to adapt once again as the Raptors stare at a roster that may still be reshaped by the pending Kawhi Leonard deal, a transaction that has hovered over this franchise like a storm cloud for weeks. The season is finished - Toronto's 2025-26 record is in the books - and the focus now is fit, not fallout. Barrett, Scottie Barnes and the incoming Collin Murray-Boyles are the pieces that matter, because this team needs more than talent; it needs clean hierarchy and sturdier pick-and-roll chemistry. Training camp in late September will show whether the new mix can breathe together or merely coexist.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The air is already turning at Commanders camp - less celebration, more accounting. The hard truth from Philadelphia was a 24-22 loss and an 0-1 start, and that's the kind of bruise that follows a team into September. Dan Quinn's club showed enough bite to suggest the roster isn't broken, but not enough polish to pretend everything is fine. Jayden Daniels still looks like the franchise's hinge point, while Luke McCaffrey's fading role is the sort of quiet alarm bell veterans notice before the public does. Washington now sits with the season in hand and the work ahead: get the offense cleaner, decide who belongs in the passing rotation, and stop wasting good enough talent. The next checkpoint is the trip to Dallas - where the Commanders will learn quickly whether this is a reset or just another tease.

article.title: Monday's Skate
paragraphs: John Chayka is describing the Maple Leafs' hectic offseason as a real obligation, while The Leafs Nation is already framing Anthony Stolarz's 2026-27 season as a test of success. For the Blue Jays, Sportsnet is still sorting out the biggest stretch-run questions, even as the Orioles come to Toronto for a game thread that puts the focus on the day ahead.

RJ Barrett's next adjustment is the Raptors' fresh talking point at Raptors Republic, with Raptors HQ also pushing readers to its new SB Nation app. In Washington, the Commanders are coming off a Week 1 loss to the Eagles, and Luke McCaffrey's role has slipped to a worrying new low, which makes the Monday read a little sharper around the margins of the roster.
